Title: Sequence of P-adic Integers has Convergent Subsequence/Lemma 1
P2
Let $\struct {\Q_p, \norm {\,\cdot\,}_p}$ be the [[Definition:Valued Field of P-adic Numbers|$p$-adic numbers]] for some [[Definition:Prime Number|prime]] $p$.
P3
Let $\sequence{x_n}$ be a [[Definition:Sequence|sequence]] of [[Definition:P-adic Integer|$p$-adic integers]].
P4
Then there exists a [[Definition:P-adic Digit|$p$-adic digit]] $b_0$ such that:
P5

:there exists [[Definition:Infinite|infinitely many]] $n \in \N$ such that the [[Definition:Canonical P-adic Expansion|canonical expansion]] of $x_n$ begins with the [[Definition:P-adic Digit|$p$-adic digit]] $b_0$
Let there exist $b \in \set{0, 1, \ldots , p - 2}$:

:there exists [[Definition:Infinite|infinitely many]] $n \in \N$ such that the [[Definition:Canonical P-adic Expansion|canonical expansion]] of $y_n$ begins with the [[Definition:P-adic Digit|$p$-adic digits]] $b$
Let $b_0 = b$ and  the result holds.
{{qed|lemma}}
For all $b \in \set{0, 1, \ldots , p - 2}$:

:there exists only a [[Definition:Finite|finite number]] of $n \in \N$ such that the [[Definition:Canonical P-adic Expansion|canonical expansion]] of $x_n$ begins with the [[Definition:P-adic Digit|$p$-adic digit]] $b$
So:

:$\set{n \in \N : \mathop \exists b \in \set{0, 1, \ldots , p - 2} : \text{ the canonical expansion  of } x_n \text{ begins with the } p \text{-adic digit } b}$ is a [[Definition:Finite Set|finite set]].
Let:
:$N = \max \set{n \in \N : \mathop \exists b \in \set{0, 1, \ldots , p - 2} : \text{ the canonical expansion  of } x_n \text{ begins with the } p \text{-adic digits } b}$
Hence for all $n > N$ and $b \in \set{0, 1, \ldots , p - 2}$:
:$x_n$ does not begin with the $p$-adic digits $b$.
So for all $n > N$:
:the [[Definition:Canonical P-adic Expansion|canonical expansion]] of $y_n$ begins with the [[Definition:P-adic Digit|$p$-adic digit]] $p-1$
Let $b_0 = p - 1$ and the result follows.
{{qed}}
